_transcription: PAGE MAP — 12 rendered pages (idx 0..11 = printed folios 1..12), every one accounted for. idx 0 = bilingual cover (Series AABB3/1, SET-3, Q.P. Code 56/1/3, 'CHEMISTRY (Theory)', Time allowed 2 hours, Maximum Marks 35, '12 printed pages'). ENGLISH = the EVEN indices 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 (folios 3, 5, 7, 9, 11). HINDI = the ODD indices 1, 3, 5, 7, 9 (folios 2, 4, 6, 8, 10). idx 11 (folio 12) is BLANK at full size — a rule, an asterisk and the footer ('56/1/3', '221 C', '12') and nothing else; NO scanner show-through this time, unlike 56/1/1 whose idx 11 ghosts folio 11. The alternating hypothesis held exactly, with NO parity inversion: I montaged the top ~14-24% of all five odd indices and every one opens in HINDI (idx 1 Hindi General Instructions + Q1, idx 3 Hindi Q2, idx 5 Hindi Q6, idx 7 Hindi Q9, idx 9 Hindi Q12 passage) — there is NO English overflow onto any odd top. English flows continuously Q1 -> Q12 across the five English pages: idx 2 = General Instructions + SECTION-A header + Q1; idx 4 = Q2, Q3 + SECTION-B header + Q4(a)/(b), Q5(a)/(b); idx 6 = Q6, Q7(a)/(b), Q8(a)/(b); idx 8 = Q9, Q10, Q11 + SECTION-C header + Q12 passage paragraph 1; idx 10 = Q12 passage paragraphs 2-3 + sub-parts (a)-(d) + the (d) OR branch. Q12 is the only question split across a page boundary. STRUCTURE — read off the paper's own printed English General Instructions on idx 2 and it matches `term2_sci` EXACTLY: (i) 12 questions, all compulsory; (ii) three Sections A, B and C; (iii) Section-A Q.Nos. 1 to 3 very short answer, 2 marks each; (iv) Section-B Q.Nos. 4 to 11 short answer, 3 marks each; (v) Section-C Q.No. 12 case based, 5 marks; (vi) log tables and calculators NOT allowed. 6 + 24 + 5 = 35, matching the cover's Maximum Marks 35 and the marking scheme's 'A full scale of marks 0-35 has to be used'. ⚠ DISAGREEMENT with the dispatch's assumption: there are only SIX printed instructions and NONE mentions internal choice — instruction (vi), which the brief says announces it on a 2022 term2 paper, is the log-tables line here. So the paper announces NO count and the marking scheme is the only authority. I walked all four scheme answer pages (ms/p02..p05) question by question: a bare 'OR' on its own line is reprinted for Q4, Q5, Q7, Q8 and for sub-part Q12(d), and for NO other question. That is 5 internal choices, each confirmed against a printed 'OR' on the paper itself (idx 4 twice, idx 6 twice, idx 10 once), and all 5 are ingested as paired rows. Q9 prints (a) and (b) with NO 'OR' between them and a combined '2 + 1 = 3'; the scheme confirms it by giving both parts under one '9.' row with no OR — so Q9 is ONE question with two sub-parts, not a choice. ⚠ DECIMAL POINTS — THE PAPER DISAGREES WITH ITS OWN MARKING SCHEME, and I followed the PAPER as the addendum requires. The paper prints ORDINARY BASELINE full stops: verified at 5x on '76.3 S cm^2 mol^-1' (idx 8) and at 6x on '[Given : log 2 = 0.3010, log 10 = 1]' (idx 8), where the decimal dot sits level with the LOWER dot of the neighbouring colon. The marking scheme is internally inconsistent: ms/p04 prints RAISED dots in Q9 ('1·55 V', '76·3', '152·6', '258·6') and ORDINARY ones in Q11 ('0.693', '2.303', '132.9'). So no `{\cdot}` is used for any decimal here. The one middle dot that IS transcribed as \cdot is the abbreviation separator in 'Conc . NaOH' on idx 10 (and the hydrate separator in NiCl2.6H2O on idx 6), both genuine centre dots. NO MCQs ANYWHERE — confirmed, and this is the Chemistry shape the addendum predicts. The marking scheme has no Section-A key table at all: its Q1, Q2 and Q3 are worked subjective answers, and Q12's five sub-parts are subjective too (not the five keyed MCQs that PHYSICS prints in its Section C). Every row is `subjective`, no row carries an `answer`, and `audit:keys` has nothing to scan. NO QUESTION WAS VOIDED BY CBSE — I read all six marking-scheme pages in full (ms/p00 and ms/p01 are the 17 general evaluation instructions; ms/p02..p05 are the answer table) and there is no 'Full mark to be awarded for any option' / 'Award full mark if attempted' / 'Error in question' / 'Data given in the paper does not support the answer' note anywhere, inside Section A or outside it. The eight award-regardless-looking notes that ARE printed are all ordinary marking latitude CONDITIONAL on correct work — '(or any other correct difference)', '(Any other suitable example in each case)', '(Balancing of equation is not necessary)', '(Any other suitable reason and example)', '(Deduct ½ mark for incorrect unit or no unit)', '(Deduct ½ marks if no or incorrect unit)', '(or any other correct method)', '(Or any other correct chemical test)' — so none is a void and `_cbseVoided` is set on zero rows. MARKING SCHEME IDENTITY — confirmed by CONTENT, not by the footer: its Q1 answers this paper's three printed orderings, its Q2 answers the strong/weak electrolyte plot, its Q6(i) gives CH3-CO-CH2-CH2-CH3 (pentan-2-one), which is C5H10O and independently corroborates the printed molecular formula, and its Q7(a)(iii) gives [CoCl2(en)2]+ for Dichloridobis(ethane-1,2-diamine)cobalt(III). Header and footer both read 56/1/3 as well. OVERLAP WITH THE OPENER 56/1/1 — matched on CONTENT, never on position: 15 of my 20 rows are the opener's, and only the 5 Q12 case-study rows sit at the same question NUMBER; the other 10 all moved (my Q1 = its Q2, my Q4a/b = its Q10a/b, my Q5a/b = its Q7a/b, my Q6 = its Q9, my Q7a/b = its Q5a/b, my Q9 = its Q11, my Q11 = its Q6). Each was re-read on MY page at full size before its stem and context text were reused byte-for-byte, so those rows will dedup on content_hash rather than shipping a near-duplicate. The 5 rows unique to this set are Q2 (molar-conductivity plot), Q3 (complex reactions), Q8(a), Q8(b) and Q10 (Ti2+/Fe2+/Cu2+/Zn2+). Note my Q10 says '3d transition series' while the opener's Q4 says '3d-transition series' with a hyphen — they are genuinely different questions with different ion sets, not a transcription drift. The opener's Q1, Q3, Q4, Q8(a) and Q8(b) do not appear on this paper at all. CHAPTERS — Q4 (both branches) is Surface Chemistry, dropped by NCERT's rationalisation, and is filed on `Surface Chemistry [Outdated]`; every other question maps to one of the ten live chapters. Nothing is out of syllabus. 20 rows for 12 questions (12 primaries + 5 OR-alternatives + the 3 extra case-study sub-parts). Primary-branch marks sum to 35.

questions.stem: Why transition metals and their compounds act as good catalyst ? How is the variability in oxidation states of transition metals different from that of the non-transition metals ? Illustrate with examples.

(a) The standard Gibbs energy \((\Delta_{\mathrm{r}}\mathrm{G}^{\circ})\) for the following cell reaction is \(-300\) kJ \(\mathrm{mol^{-1}}\) :
\(\mathrm{Zn(s)} + 2\mathrm{Ag^{+}(aq)} \rightarrow \mathrm{Zn^{2+}\,(aq)} + 2\mathrm{Ag(s)}\)
Calculate \(\mathrm{E^{o}_{cell}}\) for the reaction. (Given: 1F = 96500 \(\mathrm{mol^{-1}}\))
(b) Calculate \(\lambda^{o}_{m}\) for \(\mathrm{MgCl_2}\) if \(\lambda^{o}\) values for \(\mathrm{Mg^{2+}}\) ion and \(\mathrm{Cl^{-}}\) ion are 106 S \(\mathrm{cm^2mol^{-1}}\) and 76.3 S \(\mathrm{cm^2mol^{-1}}\) respectively.
questions._flag: Two printed-notation defects, transcribed as printed. (1) The Faraday constant is given as '1F = 96500 mol^-1' — the coulomb is missing from the unit; it should be 96500 C mol^-1, as the marking scheme itself writes. (2) Part (b) asks for lowercase lambda-nought-m for MgCl2, i.e. the symbol for a single ION's limiting molar conductivity, where the electrolyte's limiting molar conductivity (capital Lambda-nought-m) is meant; the marking scheme answers with capital Lambda. Neither defect changes what is being asked.

questions.subtopic: Chemical Reactions of Aldehydes and Ketones
questions.context:
Aldehydes, ketones and carboxylic acids are some of the important classes of organic compounds containing carbonyl group. These are highly polar molecules due to higher electro-negativity of oxygen relative to carbon in the carbonyl group. Aldehydes are prepared by dehydrogenation or controlled oxidation of primary alcohols and controlled reduction of acyl halides. Ketones are prepared by oxidation of secondary alcohols and hydration of alkynes.
Aldehydes and ketones undergo nucleophilic addition reactions onto the carbonyl group but carboxylic acid does not undergo nucleophilic addition reaction. The alpha \((\alpha)\) – hydrogens of aldehydes and ketones are acidic. Therefore aldehydes and ketones having at least one \(\alpha\)-hydrogen undergo Aldol condensation.
Aldehydes are easily oxidised by mild oxidising agents such as Tollens' reagent and Fehling's reagent. Carboxylic acids are prepared by the oxidation of primary alcohols, aldehydes and by hydrolysis of nitriles. Aromatic carboxylic acids are prepared by side-chain oxidation of alkyl benzenes. Carboxylic acids are considerably more acidic than alcohols and most of simple phenols.
